title: Cohen structure theorem: a complete local ring is a quotient of a power series ring over a field or a Cohen ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring (a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated (for instance $R$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) and which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $p\ge0$ be the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$. Then there exist an integer $n\ge0$, a ring $\Lambda$ which is a field of characteristic $0$ if $p=0$ and a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] with residue characteristic $p$ if $p>0$, and a surjective ring homomorphism $\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to R$ from the formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), part (2), and the last paragraph of its proof (the map Lambda[[x_1..x_n]] -> R, x_i -> y_i for generators y_i of m, surjective by Lemma 0315 lemma-completion-generalities). The theorem says 'Lambda is either a field or a Cohen ring'; that Lambda is a field of characteristic 0 when p = 0 (a coefficient field, isomorphic to kappa) and a Cohen ring when p > 0 is the case distinction of the proof (paragraphs 1 and 2: Cohen ring from Lemma 0328 cohen-rings-exist). Part (1) is the existing node lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists.

proof.text: (Generators; separatedness.) Since $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, choose $n\ge0$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathfrak m$ generating $\mathfrak m$ ($n=0$ when $\mathfrak m=0$). Write $r:R\to\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$ for the reduction. For every $k\ge1$ the ideal $\mathfrak m^k$ is generated by the monomials $y^E=y_1^{e_1}\cdots y_n^{e_n}$ with $|E|=e_1+\cdots+e_n=k$ (a product of $k$ elements $\sum_ic_iy_i$ expands into such monomials with coefficients in $R$). Since the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_kR/\mathfrak m^k$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], in particular injective, $\bigcap_{k\ge1}\mathfrak m^k=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, last paragraph: 'if $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ are generators of the ideal $\mathfrak m$'

proof.text: (Case $p=0$: the coefficient field.) By [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists] $R$ has a coefficient ring: a subring $\Lambda\subseteq R$ which is local with maximal ideal $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m$, with $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m=p\Lambda=0$, and such that $\Lambda=\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)\to R/\mathfrak m=\kappa$ is an isomorphism. A local ring whose maximal ideal is $0$ is a field, so $\Lambda$ is a field; it is isomorphic to $\kappa$, which has characteristic $p=0$, so $\Lambda$ is a field of characteristic $0$. Let $\alpha:\Lambda\to R$ be the inclusion; then $r\circ\alpha:\Lambda\to\kappa$ is surjective (it is the isomorphism above).

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraph 1 (the image of $\lim_n\varphi_n:\kappa\to R$, the coefficient field), as stated in part (1)

proof.text: (Case $p>0$: a Cohen ring and compatible maps $\varphi_k$.) As $p\cdot1\mapsto0$ in $\kappa$, $p\in\mathfrak m$, so $p^k=0$ in $D_k=R/\mathfrak m^k$ for every $k\ge1$. For $k\ge2$ let $\pi_k:R/\mathfrak m^k\to R/\mathfrak m^{k-1}$ be the projection; its kernel $J_k=\mathfrak m^{k-1}/\mathfrak m^k$ has $J_k^2=0$ since $2k-2\ge k$, and $\pi_k$ identifies $D_k/J_k$ with $R/\mathfrak m^{k-1}$. Let $r_k:R/\mathfrak m^k\to\kappa$ be the reduction. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist] choose a Cohen ring $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] (a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$, $p\Lambda$-adically complete) and a ring isomorphism $\varepsilon:\Lambda/p\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa$; its residue field $\Lambda/p\Lambda\cong\kappa$ has characteristic $p$. Let $\rho_k:\Lambda/p^k\Lambda\to\Lambda/p^{k-1}\Lambda$ and $\sigma_k:\Lambda/p^k\Lambda\to\Lambda/p\Lambda$ be the reductions. We construct ring homomorphisms $\varphi_k:\Lambda/p^k\Lambda\to R/\mathfrak m^k$ with $\pi_k\circ\varphi_k=\varphi_{k-1}\circ\rho_k$ ($k\ge2$) and $r_k\circ\varphi_k=\varepsilon\circ\sigma_k$. Put $\varphi_1=\varepsilon$. Given $\varphi_{k-1}$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-mod-pn-formally-smooth] (the ring map $\mathbf Z/p^k\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^k\Lambda$ is formally smooth) to $D=D_k$ (with $p^kD=0$), the square-zero ideal $J=J_k$ and $g=\varphi_{k-1}\circ\rho_k:\Lambda/p^k\Lambda\to R/\mathfrak m^{k-1}=D/J_k$: it gives a ring homomorphism $\varphi_k$ with $\pi_k\circ\varphi_k=\varphi_{k-1}\circ\rho_k$, and then $r_k\circ\varphi_k=r_{k-1}\circ\varphi_{k-1}\circ\rho_k=\varepsilon\circ\sigma_{k-1}\circ\rho_k=\varepsilon\circ\sigma_k$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraph 2 (choose a Cohen ring $\Lambda$ with $\kappa=\Lambda/p\Lambda$ by Lemma 0328; maps $\varphi_n:\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ by induction using Lemma 0329 cohen-ring-formally-smooth)

proof.text: (Case $p>0$: the map $\alpha:\Lambda\to R$.) For $a\in\Lambda$ the elements $\varphi_k(a\bmod p^k)\in R/\mathfrak m^k$ are compatible under the $\pi_k$ (step 3), so $a\mapsto(\varphi_k(a\bmod p^k))_k$ is a ring homomorphism $\Lambda\to\varprojlim_kR/\mathfrak m^k$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; composing with the inverse of the canonical ring isomorphism $R\to\varprojlim_kR/\mathfrak m^k$ ($R$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]) gives a ring homomorphism $\alpha:\Lambda\to R$ with $\alpha(a)\bmod\mathfrak m^k=\varphi_k(a\bmod p^k)$. For $k=1$: $r(\alpha(a))=\varepsilon(a\bmod p)$, so $r\circ\alpha:\Lambda\to\kappa$ is surjective, $\varepsilon$ being an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraph 2: 'Putting these maps together $\lim_n\varphi_n:\Lambda=\lim_n\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\to R=\lim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$' (the map $\Lambda\to R$ used in the last paragraph)

proof.text: (The map $\Phi$.) In both cases we have $n$, the ring $\Lambda$ required by the statement (a field of characteristic $0$ if $p=0$, step 2; a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ if $p>0$, step 3), and a ring homomorphism $\alpha:\Lambda\to R$ with $r\circ\alpha$ surjective (steps 2, 4). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] with $T=R$, $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m$ ($R$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete), $\alpha$, and $t_i=y_i\in\mathfrak m$: there is a ring homomorphism $\Phi:A=\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to R$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] with $\Phi(\lambda)=\alpha(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $\Phi(x_i)=y_i$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, last paragraph: 'we can use the map $\Lambda\to R$ just constructed to get a map $\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to R$, $x_i\mapsto y_i$'

proof.text: ($\Phi$ is surjective.) Regard $M=R$ as an $A$-module through $\Phi$ and let $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\subseteq A$. (1) $A$ is $I$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete]. (2) $I^k$ is generated by the monomials $x^E$ with $|E|=k$, so $I^kM$ is the ideal of $R$ generated by the $\Phi(x^E)=y^E$, $|E|=k$, which is $\mathfrak m^k$ (step 1); hence $\bigcap_kI^kM=\bigcap_k\mathfrak m^k=0$ (step 1). (3) $M/IM=R/\mathfrak m=\kappa$, on which $F\in A$ acts as multiplication by $r(\Phi(F))$; for $c\in\kappa$ choose $\lambda\in\Lambda$ with $r(\alpha(\lambda))=c$ (step 5), so $c=\lambda\cdot\bar1$ with $\bar1=1\bmod\mathfrak m$: the image of $1\in M$ generates $M/IM$ over $A/I$, which is therefore finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] (with this $A$, $I$, $M$) the element $1$ generates $M$ over $A$: every $s\in R$ is $s=F\cdot1=\Phi(F)$ for some $F\in A$. So $\Phi:\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to R$ is surjective. (Stacks argues with Lemma 0315 (1): both sides are $I$-adically complete and the map is surjective modulo $I$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] is Lemma 031D, whose proof is that application of 0315 (1), and needs only $\bigcap_kI^kM=0$ besides the completeness of $A$.)

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, last paragraph: 'Since both sides are $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$-adically complete this map is surjective by Lemma 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities) as it is surjective modulo $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ by construction'; packaged as Algebra, Lemma Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring, line 22860)
